headline: Public urged a contract for school secretaries after 491 days; district asked for $290,874.39 more for 617 Lexington Street.
summary: The district asked for $290,874.39 more for the transformer project at 617 Lexington Street, after PCB-contaminated oil was found during excavation. The original $825,000 allocation covered the dual language relocation and reuse of that building, and the item will return on the next agenda. During public comment, school secretaries said they have gone 491 days without a contract and asked for a fair offer. The committee also approved budget transfers and bills, and sent three high school schedule questions to Dr. Kanad.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including the October 21 minutes and donations.
Approved getting the survey data before the next meeting, with a vote on the calendar at that meeting.
Approved sending three high school schedule questions to Dr. Kanad.
Tabled the school committee subcommittee meetings item.
Approved three budget transfers dated November 4.
Approved paying the bills on the warrant.
discussion: Secretaries' contract: Public speakers said school secretaries have worked 491 days without a contract and asked for a fair offer. Speakers also said the district offered unions 2.5 percent.
Executive position: Public speakers said a communications role with a $140,000 salary was approved on October 21 by a four-to-three vote.

High school schedule: Speakers asked for schedule options, data, and criteria before the November 23rd forum, and for a parent seat on the scheduling committee. Members asked for a clear reason for the change, and the district said feedback counts alongside graduation standards and required programs.

Transformer project costs: Members asked how facilities and the city auditor's figures compare, and whether the work would disrupt school. Staff said most of the work happens on weekends, and the figures will be checked for an update at the next meeting.

Calendar and holiday survey: The survey drew 868 responses. 50% wanted to keep the current Labor Day and Thanksgiving schedule, and 40.7% said there should be no school on Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Good Friday.
